domain: Legal Theory / Intellectual Property / Cultural Production
topic_summary: Analysis of the fair use doctrine in copyright law as a contested kernel. The four-factor test (17 U.S.C. § 107) serves as the fixed statutory substrate, but creator-centric and user-centric interpretations read this substrate to instantiate structurally different constraints on unauthorized use, with different victim sets and base extractiveness.

key_entities: 17 U.S.C. § 107 (statutory four-factor test: purpose, nature, amount, market effect)
Rights holders / content industries (copyright owners seeking enforcement)
Transformative users (remix artists, parodists, educators, archivists)
Federal courts (interpretive authority via case law accretion)
Public domain (conceptual commons outside copyright term or scope)
DMCA anti-circumvention provisions (interacting constraint on technical access)
key_tensions: Creator compensation vs cultural commons access (incentive structure vs public goods)
Statutory clarity vs judicial discretion (rule vs standard interpretive approach)
key_mechanisms: Four-factor balancing test (purpose/character, nature of work, amount/substantiality, market harm)
Transformative use doctrine (Campbell v. Acuff-Rose 1994 interpretive layer)
Ex post litigation filtering (fair use as affirmative defense, not ex ante safe harbor)
key_absences: Algorithmic/ML training use cases (statute predates AI training paradigm)
Cross-border enforcement asymmetries (fair use is U.S.-centric; no EU equivalent)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: 17 U.S.C. § 107 four-factor test as the fixed statutory substrate for adjudicating legitimate unauthorized use
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Federal judiciary interprets the four factors via case law; Supreme Court precedent (Campbell, Google v. Oracle) sets binding interpretive norms
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Pluralism (multiple live readings coexist; no central authority enforces uniformity across circuits)

readings.commitment: Fair use is narrow exception to property right; four factors weighed to preserve creator incentives
readings.authority_grounding: Originalist (property-rights tradition); economically grounded in incentive theory
readings.expected_structural_delta: High epsilon on unauthorized use; rights holders primary beneficiary; chilling effect on derivative works; victim set = transformative users and public domain

readings.commitment: Fair use is affirmative user right; four factors weighed to preserve public access and cultural production
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low epsilon on unauthorized use; public/educational users primary beneficiary; reduced creator compensation; victim set = rights holders

readings.commitment: Transformativeness dominates four-factor balancing; market harm subordinated when use adds new meaning
readings.authority_grounding: Campbell precedent (1994); judicial doctrine favoring cultural innovation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate epsilon; context-dependent; beneficiary = remix culture and tech platforms enabling UGC; victim set shifts based on transformation threshold

axiom_contradictions.basis: Creator-centric treats copyright as property requiring compensation for any value extraction; user-centric treats culture as commons requiring access for any socially valuable use. No single framework holds both axioms simultaneously.

axes.structural_delta: The four-factor test provides no weighting formula, algorithm, or bright-line rules; judicial discretion is mandated by statute
axes.primary_observable: Variance in fair use outcomes across factually similar cases; circuit splits on factor interpretation
axes.selection_reason: Physical constraint enabling kernel structure; all readings downstream of this ambiguity

axes.structural_delta: Fair use as narrow exception; copyright as strong property right requiring compensation
axes.primary_observable: Judicial rulings emphasizing market harm (factor 4) and licensing markets; injunction grant rates
axes.selection_reason: High epsilon reading with clear beneficiary/victim structure; structurally distinct from user-centric

axes.structural_delta: Fair use as affirmative right; cultural production and education as trump cards over compensation
axes.primary_observable: Judicial rulings emphasizing transformative purpose (factor 1) and First Amendment values; dismissal rates of infringement claims
axes.selection_reason: Epsilon contrast with creator-centric; axiom contradiction declared

axes.structural_delta: Campbell precedent elevates transformativeness; market harm subordinated when new meaning/message added
axes.primary_observable: Citation frequency of Campbell in fair use opinions; outcomes in parody/commentary/UGC cases
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: hybrid position between creator/user poles; lower structural distinctiveness; captured as omega variable

axes.human_readable: Ex Post Litigation Filter (Fair Use as Affirmative Defense)
axes.structural_delta: Fair use determinable only after infringement lawsuit filed; no ex ante safe harbor
axes.primary_observable: Chilling effect metrics (self-censorship surveys, abandoned projects); litigation cost vs. licensing cost comparison
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: enforcement mechanism snare; high epsilon but procedurally distinct from interpretive readings

axes.human_readable: Algorithmic Training Use Absence (Statute Predates AI Paradigm)
axes.structural_delta: ML training on copyrighted corpora not addressed by 1976 statute or Supreme Court precedent
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of AI training fair use claims in litigation (2023-present); judicial uncertainty in opinions
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: emerging issue; statute lacks clear anchor; omega frontier

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Hybrid reading between creator/user poles; lower structural independence; captured in omega for third-reading expansion

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Fair use as affirmative defense requiring litigation
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Enforcement mechanism distinct from interpretive readings; chilling effect subordinated to reading-level epsilon contrast

deferred_axes.structural_delta: ML training paradigm unaddressed by statute or precedent
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Emerging frontier; no settled doctrine; omega variable pending future case law

omegas.description: Transformative use doctrine may be third reading rather than hybrid. If Campbell shifts from interpretive gloss to independent constraint, expand to three-reading generation.
Algorithmic training on copyrighted corpora is statute-external. If courts create new doctrine rather than apply four-factor test, kernel structure may fracture.
omegas.source: Deferred axis algorithmic_training_absence + Dark Matter Probe 2

omegas.description: DMCA anti-circumvention provisions bypass fair use analysis for technical access. Ex post litigation filter may be subordinate to ex ante technical constraint.

omegas.description: Fair use is U.S.-centric; EU fair dealing / InfoSoc Directive instantiates different kernel. Cross-border enforcement may reveal fair use as piton of U.S. jurisdiction rather than mountain of copyright theory.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: statutory_ambiguity_substrate classified as mountain (physical constraint on judicial interpretation) but may be piton of Congressional drafting choice. If Congress could amend § 107 with algorithmic weighting, mountain collapses to rope. Generated omega_ai_training_frontier and omega_international_kernel_variance to bound this uncertainty.
